newsitem.title: FRANCE: France closes Hard Rock Cafe over mad cow fears.`
newsitem.headline: France closes Hard Rock Cafe over mad cow fears.`

text.p: Police closed down the Hard Rock Cafe in Paris for two weeks from Wednesday, saying the restaurant had imported beef from Britain in defiance of a ban imposed due to fears over mad cow disease.

The restaurant, on Paris' Boulevard Montmartre, has argued the 300 kg (660 lbs) of frozen hamburgers seized last week by health inspectors came legally from cows raised in Ireland and had merely been processed in Britain.
Paris police headquarters cited a danger of "serious risks for public health" in ordering the restaurant closed.
The Hard Rock Cafe, one of an American-style chain owned by the Rank Organisation, declined immediate comment.
After examining the restaurant's import documents for the beef, "the ministry of Agriculture...confirmed that the import to France of the beef seized on October 28 was illegal."
It said the closure was a simple administrative measure that did not affect possible court action against the restaurant.

France led a worldwide ban on imports of British beef in March this year over fears that mad cow disease, or Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), could be passed to humans. BSE is most widespread in Britain.
Almost a year before the beef import ban was imposed, health inspectors seized 500 kg (1,100 lbs) of British minced beef in the restaurant that lacked required health stamps, police said.
